newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian consumer sentiment falls in Feb.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian consumer sentiment falls in Feb.

text.p: Westpac Banking Corp said on Wednesday its consumer confidence index fell 8.7 points or 7.9 percent in February.

The index now stands at 101.2, the lowest level since September 996. The index series history was revised in the February release, using new seasonal adjustment factors based on data from 1986 to 1996.

Westpac's general manager of economics, Bill Evans, said the series had been volatile since last November, when it rose by 8.1 percent, then fell by 5.3 percent in December, only to rise by 6.0 percent in January and then fall heavily again.

"In the past, such oscillations have generally preceded major sharp sustained movements in the index," Evans said in a statement, adding that in 1993 the index showed similar volatility before rising sharply in the final quarter.
The February fall mainly reflected a fall in consumer expectations for economic conditions over the coming year, Evans said.
However, Westpac's believes there are some early signs, particularly in housing, that better conditions could be expected in 1997.
As a result, this index component was expected to begin to improve, and there is a good chance the index will be higher through 1997, Evans said.

"Based on some recent public comments from the Governor of the Reserve Bank, it appears the Reserve Bank has seen signs of some improvements in the economy in housing, employment and investment," he said, adding this meant it was very unlikely the Bank would cut rates in the next few months.
"Beyond that, we expect there will be encouraging signs for the Bank to hold off on any changes to rates for the remainder of 1997," Evans said. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
